original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: All direct and reverse titrations were performed on a Microcal ITC200 instrument at 20 and 37 °C. Subnanomolar affinity of bevacizumab/VEGF binding was also measured on a Microcal VP-ITC at 20 °C. Bevacizumab was obtained from 25 mg/mL of biosimilar Aybintio (Samsung). The buffer was exchanged for ITC buffer by successive ultrafiltration/dilution steps. The molar absorbance was calculated from the sequence (ε280nm = 243 340 M−1 cm−1). Lyophilized peptides and VEGF were dissolved in ITC buffer (HEPES/NaOH 50 mM, NaCl 150 mM, pH 7.52), then vortexed, centrifuged, and filtered (0.1 μm) to prepare stock solutions. We note that all of the peptides were freely soluble up to 1 mM. Diluted samples were degassed, and concentrations were measured by UV (SpectraMax Quickdrop Spectrophotometer) in triplicate following the previously published ITC titration procedure.19 Briefly, several precautions must be taken for titration design: (i) an optimal “c-value” (the Wiseman parameter44) must be chosen between 30 and 500, (ii) an inflection curve centered on half-term of titration, and (iii) the absolute value of the second titration peak should be close to 0.5–1.5 μcal/s in order to get a high signal/noise ratio. The running parameters set for monomer peptides were as follows. Sixteen injections were done for each titration. The volume of the first small injection was set to 0.5 μL, and it was set to 2.54 μL for the 15 main injections. The reference power was set as 5 μcal/s, the initial delay was 60 s, and the stirring speed was 800 rpm. The delay between two injections was 200 s. For titrations of dimer peptides, all parameters were kept the same except that 14 injections were done for each titration. The volume of the first injection was set to 0.35 μL, and it was set to 2.94 μL for the 13 main injections. For each peptide, ITC raw data were integrated by NITPIC45,46 and globally analyzed in SEDPHAT.25 AB Hetero-Association model and ABB Two Symmetric sites model were applied to dimer peptide binding with VEGF and monomer peptide binding with VEGF, respectively. The fixed (2:1 or 1:1) stoichiometry implies refining a concentration correction factor for each titration. The enthalpy of binding was normalized by fixing the correction of protein concentration for reverse titrations to 1.000. The confidence intervals were estimated at confidence level P = 95% with F-statistics-based contours of the error surface implemented in SEDPHAT, with the titrant molecule correction factor set, baseline, and correction factor of the titrated molecule being floating. Finally, GUSSI was used to output the illustrations of thermograms.47

original_paragraph.Table 2 data: Table 2 presents the thermodynamic parameters for binding at 20 °C and 37 °C. For example, at 20 °C, the Kd for D6 is 9 [5, 15] nM, ΔG° is -10.8 [-11.1, -10.5] kcal mol−1, ΔH° is -37.5 [-38.4, -36.7] kcal mol−1, -TΔS° is 26.7 [25.6, 27.9] kcal mol−1, nd/nr is 2:2, and ΔCp is -0.75 [-0.85, -0.65] kcal mol−1 K−1. At 37 °C, the Kd for D6 is 26 [16, 41] nM, ΔG° is -10.8 [-11.1, -10.5] kcal mol−1, ΔH° is -50.3 [-51.8, -48.8] kcal mol−1, -TΔS° is 39.5 [37.7, 41.4] kcal mol−1, nd/nr is 2:2, and ΔCp is -0.86 [-0.98, -0.74] kcal mol−1 K−1.
original_paragraph.Figure 2 thermogram data: The thermograms in Figure 2 show the following values for dimer D6: Direct titration at 20°C: Kd = 12 nM, ΔH = -38.6 kcal/mol, ΔS = -95.4 cal/mol K. Reverse titration at 20°C: Kd = 11 nM, ΔH = -37.4 kcal/mol, ΔS = -91.1 cal/mol K. Direct titration at 37°C: Kd = 26 nM, ΔH = -50.2 kcal/mol, ΔS = -127 cal/mol K. Reverse titration at 37°C: Kd = 14 nM, ΔH = -50.6 kcal/mol, ΔS = -127 cal/mol K.
